title: Gulliver and the Art of Satire
objective: After this level you can explain why satire uses exaggeration to criticize, using Gulliver's Travels.
summary: Swift's Gulliver's Travels (1726) shrinks real quarrels to egg wars and heel parties in tiny Lilliput. Satire exaggerates what it mocks until the familiar looks absurd.

cards.headline: Eleven thousand people died rather than crack an egg at the wrong end.
cards.body: That's the grim history Gulliver hears in Lilliput, where a law ordered everyone to break their eggs at the smaller end. It is computed, he's told, that "eleven thousand persons" have died rather than obey. Ridiculous? That's exactly the point.

cards.headline: Four strange voyages
cards.body: Jonathan Swift's Gulliver's Travels appeared anonymously in 1726. Its hero sails to Lilliput, where people stand less than 6 inches tall; to Brobdingnag, a land of giants; to Laputa, a flying island; and finally to a land where rational horses, the Houyhnhnms, rule over brutish humanlike creatures, the Yahoos.

cards.headline: Small people, small quarrels
cards.body: Lilliput's egg war mocks the religious quarrels of Swift's day, and its two political parties, told apart by high or low heels, stand for England's Tories and Whigs. The Lilliputians' tiny size mirrors their small-mindedness. Swift doesn't argue that the quarrels are petty. He shrinks them until you can see it for yourself.
cards.callout: Shrink a quarrel, and its pettiness shows.

cards.headline: The trick of satire
cards.body: Satire holds vices and follies up to ridicule, through irony, parody or caricature. The satirist exaggerates what's objectionable, so readers see the absurd in the familiar. Swift even turns it on his own country. After Gulliver proudly describes England, the king of Brobdingnag calls its people "the most pernicious race of little odious vermin that nature ever suffered to crawl upon the surface of the earth."

questions.prompt: In Lilliput, the two political parties are told apart by _____.

options.label: which end of an egg they break
the color of their hats
options.rationale: Nothing in the level says so.

questions.explanation: Lilliput's parties are told apart by high or low heels, standing for England's Tories and Whigs.

questions.prompt: Why does Swift shrink real quarrels into fights over eggs and heels?

options.label: He was writing a children's story with no targets
options.rationale: The egg war and heels mock real quarrels.

options.label: Exaggeration makes familiar quarrels look absurd
Lilliput was a real country he had visited
Eggs were a real cause of war in England
options.rationale: The eggs stand for religious quarrels.

questions.explanation: Satire exaggerates what it mocks: shrunk to eggs and heels, real religious and political quarrels show how petty they are.

questions.prompt: Level 2's fables use animals that act like humans to poke at human follies. Which part of Gulliver's Travels does something similar?

options.label: Lilliput's egg law
options.rationale: The Lilliputians are tiny people, not animals.

options.label: The land of the rational horses, the Houyhnhnms

questions.explanation: Like a fable's talking animals, Swift's rational horses rule over brutish humanlike Yahoos, turning an animal story into a mirror for people.
